Name: Jo Welch
Question: Does vinegar and water prevent lice?
Answer: Shampoos containing heavy tea tree oil fragrance can deter lice infestations. Lice also like clean hair and scalps. The less debris there is on the scalp and hair the easier it is for them to move around on the scalp and attach their nits to hair strands. Oily hair and dirty scalps deter lice just as effectively as tea tree oil. Vinegar and water will have no effect on the lice or their nits. If you already have lice, you must use a lice shampoo and a nit comb to remove lice and nits. Lice shampoo contains an insecticide and you must follow instructions in in order to use it safely.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: I always see 'do not use this on your eyebrows' warning on box dyes. I want to dye my eyebrows along with my hair however. So what exactly happens if I use it on my eyebrows?
Answer: It is what happens long term that is scary. Sure if you accidentally get it in your eyes you risk the chance of blindness. But what if you are careful? The tissue around your eyes is very thin and can easily absorb chemicals - penetrating the areas around the eyeball and optic nerves. If you are using permanent dye designed to use for hair coloring and the label states not to use it anywhere else, please take heed to the warning. Over time you can get blurred vision, but by then you have totally forgotten about the times you used hair color on your eyebrows. The damage to the nerves in the eyes caused by tissue absorption is done. It starts with blurred vision and gets worse over time. There is no way to correct it. Only use dyes labeled Lash & Brow Tint on your eyebrows. Refectocil is one of the few that is deemed by the FDA.

Question: I used color oops and now my hair is orange. Should I bleach it or will toner permanently take out the orange? I want it back to black.
Answer: If it is a nice deep orange you can use black with 10 volume and the orange will be your filler. You may need to add a little dark red to the black color. The only way to really nail it is to do some strand tests first before applying black color all over.

Question: Why is it that people expect a break on price when they ask you to come to their house to do their hair? Any other profession that made a house call would be much more than an office visit.
Answer: Most people who are not in our industry think that if we come and do their hair at their home we are doing it on the side and under the table. I personally have only done house calls when there has been someone who is unable to make it to the salon for health reasons. It has been a long time since I've done it but I charged a mileage rate and an off-site surcharge along with the regular cost the service would have been if they come to the salon. When you go to someone's home it's very inconvenient. You have to pack up everything from the salon and take it with you and then unpack it when you get there. They may or may not have good lighting which compromises your work. They may or may not have good seating for them which compromises your work. It's a real pain to go to someone's home versus have them come into the salon. Maybe the easiest thing to do is have an off-site menu that explains the mileage and surcharge for time involved prepping to do the service. Think about it, when they come in the salon everything is there, all they have to do is walk back and sit in your chair. When you go to their house it is a process to unpack, find good lighting get their service done and then repack everything and drive back. Then when you get back to the salon you have to unpack and clean all your tools and put them back in your station. This is why I only did it for my long standing clients who had health issues which kept them from coming in from time to time. Do not sell yourself short. You have a craft and you're worth what you are worth.

Question: I dyed my hair dark brown and it turned black. Can I dye it the next day chestnut brown to look lighter?
Answer: Hair color is not bleach. And sadly, hair color will not lighten artificial dye. You are going to have to do something a little more aggressive. There are several things you can do but there's no guarantee on the outcome without having someone who is knowledgeable in color correction do it for you. You may try a soap cap first. Mix 1 oz of hair bleach, 1 oz of shampoo and 1 oz of 20 volume developer. If you have thick long hair you may need to increase the amounts but it is equal parts of all three ingredients. Wet your hair down thoroughly with very warm water and massage this mixture into your hair for up to 5 minutes. The sooner you do it after a fresh color the more likely it is to work. It can lift anywhere from one to two levels and you may have to repeat the procedure if you don't get enough lift in that 5 minutes. This is not something you apply to your hair and just leave it on your hair for 5 minutes. You must use your fingers and the palms of your hands to scrub to make sure into the hair shafts. This mechanical movement combined with the chemical application is going to be what does the trick. Before you apply a soap Cap all over your head. Makes a very small amount of the three ingredients in equal parts and take a section of hair about a pencil with in diameter. Apply the mixture the way I stated above to do a strand test to see if it will even lift the hair color. If the procedure works you've got options here. Sometimes the procedure by itself can lift enough and you may not need to recolor. But most likely you're going to get enough lift but it's going to look spotty and you will need to go back over it with your lighter brown color formulation. Hope this helps. For those of you reading this, color will not lift hair color. It will only lift hair that has no artificial dye on it whatsoever. Even on natural hair with no color, hair dyes only have the ability to lift up to four levels. But this does not pertain to hair that is anywhere from black to dark brown. The rule applies to natural hair that is a level 5 and lighter. Level five Falls around a medium brown on a color leveling system which counts to level 11. If you're using a color system that counts to a level 12 it may be one level darker (6) that will lift up to four levels.

Question: What's the best way to split up with your hairdresser if she's given you the wrong style/colour the last four times?
Answer: Don't go back. You're not in a contractual agreement with the individual who is not getting your hair right. Do what you need to do for you. You have to wear your hair everyday. It is a big blow to the self-esteem when you don't feel like you look your best.

Question: What are some tips for promoting hair growth after a bad haircut? How can you fix mistakes when cutting your own hair?
Answer: Well, when it comes to Speedy growth you're just going to have to let mother nature take its course. Meaning hair grows approximately one half an inch per month. Not much is going to change that. Do the math and you'll know about when it's going to grow out enough to your satisfaction. As far as repairing a bad haircut you want to leave that to the professionals. Sometimes you cannot repair it and have to be patient and let it grow out more. If you are the one who did the bad haircut you might want to refrain from working on your hair again. If it was done by a professional, you can go back to the business and complain to the manager or owner and see if someone other than the person who did the damage will fix it. This usually will be done at no charge to save face for the business. Hope you're able to get it corrected soon there's nothing worse than walking around with a bad haircut and not feeling good about yourself because of it.

Question: Is baby oil good for hair? Are there any techniques to use it on hair?
Answer: Mineral oil is a petroleum by-product and should not be used on the hair for any purpose. If you by chance have hair color it will speed up fading and over time you can get a drying effect from the mineral oil. Use something like rosehip oil, coconut oil, Moroccan oil in small amounts. No oil has moisturizing properties but if you use a good moisturizer for your hair and then follow up with a few drops of oil, it will seal in the benefits of the moisturizer you used prior. Some oils such as olive oil can actually attract microbes to the hair and scalp. We actually use olive oil in the lab in Petri dishes to grow stuff.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How can you politely ask your hair stylist to clean their tools before using them on you?
Answer: If you are getting a haircut and they are using Clippercide, ask them to give the blades and guards an extra spray. Ask them if they are diligent in following DBPR guidelines for sanitation. Legally they should be sanitizing and sterilizing every item they use before using them on a new customer. They should have a closed drawer with clean items stored for use on each new client and a closed drawer or container keeping soiled and used tools isolated until they can clean them, immerse them in Barbicide or Marvicide and rinse them. Pay attention to how they are using the cutting cape. Even if the cape is new and clean, it cannot touch bare skin. There should be either a clean towel or Sanek strip put around your neck first. Sanek strips are the little white paper, stretchy strips. All these precautions are in place and have been for decades, prior to COVID and are to protect you from blood born viruses/diseases and contact - cross contamination from skin diseases and infections. You have the right to ask/request. I have been in the business for 50 years and know better. They should know better too. It is one of the reasons they must go to school to get proper training and take and keep a valid Barber/Cosmetology license to practice their craft.

Question: What will happen if I put orange over black hair dye?
Answer: Not much. Orange is much lighter than black. The black will overpower the orange pigment. I doubt you would even be able to see it in bright sunlight. Black can be levels 1 through 3. Orange is present in lighter levels such and dark blonde, level 7.

Question: Can orange hair dye cover up blue hair dye?
Answer: Probably not. Orange and blue are opposite each other on the color wheel, when you combine both these colors together you will get Brown, not orange. If it were an oxidative dye they would probably neutralize each other out really well to a natural Brown. But I have a feeling you are using direct dye over the top of another direct dye. You can do a strand test and see if it works before you put it all over. That is what we have to do in the salon when we are not sure of the outcome.

Question: What is the recommended time to leave semi-permanent hair dye on your head? Is it safe to sleep with the dye on or should it be washed out immediately?
Answer: Follow the instructions on the label. Every semi-permanent color manufacturer can have slightly different instructions. If it contains any type of developer where you mix color with another ingredient you probably shouldn't be sleeping with it on your head overnight. Direct dyes that contain no hydrogen peroxide additive can stay on the hair longer but you risk having allergic reactions or skin reactions. Follow the instructions on the label.

Question: Is a sulfate-free shampoo formulation needed?
Answer: Sulfate free shampoos are generally recommended when a person has a chemical service on their hair. This could be anything from hair color to a straightener. Sulfate-free shampoos are more gentle but they do not remove debris easily. If you do not have any chemical services on your hair feel free to use a regular shampoo that is not sulfate free. If you are using a sulfate free shampoo it's recommended that you shampoo at least once every seven times with a clarifying shampoo. Especially if you use a lot of products on your hair because the sulfate-free shampoos are not strong enough to remove buildup.

Question: What does a LICE check at school detect? Does it only look for nits and larvae, or can it also detect adult live head lice?
Answer: They will be looking for all three. But the easiest to spot are the nits because they are little white particles that attach to the hair shaft. Lice on the scalp depending on the color of lice and the scalp may not be as easy to see. And they can move too. As well as larvae they move also. Lice can range in color from a pale tan to darker brown.

Question: Why is my hair getting darker on the ends? My natural color is a dark brown. I dye my hair red so every so often I have to touch up my root but, the hair color difference in the red in my roots and my ends is very different. Why does this happen.
Answer: If you are applying the color from Roots to ends every time you do your retouch this will definitely cause the ends to get darker. Every time you reapply color to previously colored hair it will darken the midshaft and ends to where they never look like the new growth. I don't know if this is what you're doing but if it is, stop it. The only hair you need to be applying color to is your new growth. Obviously your ends aren't fading because they're holding on to color on top of color. Just color your new growth and keep cutting the ends and eventually it'll be the same color from Roots to end provided you using exactly the same color and processing it exactly the same timing. I've seen novice colorist do this. Someone will come in for a retouch and the colors will do what we call pull the color through the ends. Then I get a call three retouches later and they want to know why the color isn't coloring The Roots anymore. Well, then you growth is turning the perfect color that it was the first time it was ever done and the rest of it is getting overlapped high concentrations of pigment on overly processed hair. Hope this helps.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: If appearantly white hair glistens somewhat yellow in sunlight, it is probably pale blonde hair. What color would actual white hair shimmer in sunlight?
Answer: Whether it's high lift white blonde hair or white gray hair there is going to be some yellow pigment. The yellow pigment is the underlying pigment in all white hair. If the yellow pigment is gone the hair is gone. What do I mean by that? As we start from dark going to light the hair shifts from dark red to Red Brown then to red orange. The shift continues as we go lighter from red orange to Orange then to yellow orange and finally yellow. Yellow pigment exists in all hair color and it is the smallest color pigment in natural hair. It is deeper in the cortex than any other color and why it does not come out completely. If someone bleaches their hair to a pale blonde and tries to take it all the way to White, the hair will dissolve before all the yellow is removed. And this is why toners are so popular. We use toners to mask the yellow and pale yellow pigments when bleaching hair up to a blonde or pale blonde.

Question: Hi I just recently got a perm and saw you answered to a question about a perm before. When you said that you sprayed with a bottle all around your hair after that did you ad anything into your hair so it wouldn’t get as frizzy again?
Answer: After you shampoo your hair and condition it. Towel dry well completely detangle your hair with a comb. You should be letting your hair air dry and not brushing it. If you brush a perm it's going to look big poofy and Frizzy. If you still find after letting an air dry that you have frizziness you might want to use some curl cream. There are a ton of Manufacturers that make curl cream. What curl cream does is it calms down the frizzies but you still have the curl pattern. Using a spray bottle on the days you don't want to shampoo or wet down your hair in the shower, is in essence waiting down your hair so you can detangle it again scrunch it with your fingers and let it dry natural. You can use a pic or a comb to lift it but you don't want to separate the curls much or again you get the frizziness. Hope this helps. Sometimes it's difficult to explain things when you don't have someone right in front of you and you can see their hair to know what's going on.

Question: Does purple shampoo emphasise natural blond highlights?
Answer: Purple shampoo is used to neutralize yellow in pale blonde hair and white gray hair. So, if your natural blonde highlights or a little too warm for your liking purple shampoo may be a good fix. Sometimes you need to use it more than once as it has a cumulative effect. When you get it to the tone you like, back off and use your regular shampoo until you see the tone starting to fade again. Using it daily can cause a purple cast to the hair. But can easily be remedied by backing off and using your normal shampoo then alternating as you see necessary.

Question: What do old, retired people typically do all day if not well off financially?

I squat and bench press, etc. We train every body part on a 3 day split. I just installed a pull-up bar in my house. My goal is to be able to do pull ups by August. I have been earning my Masters in Cosmetic Chemistry and I should graduate next spring. I stay involved in my community and a couple of non profit ventures to help low income pet owners find affordable spay and neuter programs for their fur babies. I live in a beach town. Question: Can I sue or press charges on my hair dresser for braiding my daughter’s hair too tight?

Name: Jo Welch
Question: I have 4a hair and oil it constantly, but I still get so much dandruff. Why is this?
Answer: Do you have dandruff or do you have dry scalp? If you have true dandruff you should not be using oil. Unless it is tea tree oil. Tea tree oil contains antimicrobial properties that can control dandruff. Any other types of oils could actually make it worse by feeding the microbes. If you have dry scalp, oils do not moisturize. They can be applied over the top of moisturizers to hold them in but they do not create moisture in any way shape or form. Another thing that could be happening may have to do with the frequency or infrequency of how often you shampoo your hair. If you are shampooing once a week or twice a month, you are more likely to have a buildup of dead skin cells because you are not removing them on a regular basis. This could be corrected my shampooing more often and brushing your hair all the way to the scalp regularly. If you are not sure what the condition is that you have on your scalp, see a dermatologist versus taking recommendations from any of us who cannot see and analyze your scalp in person. Hope you can get it taken care of.

Question: Does the colour of bleached facial hair wear off?
Answer: It cannot wear off because bleaching is the process of removing all pigment from the hair. If the pigment is gone it cannot come back naturally. You can use a Dye specifically for dying beards. Or, you can wait until it grows out and shave it off. Whatever you do, do not use hair color used for the head on your facial hair.

Question: What is the most effective oil for reducing dandruff? Is coconut, olive, or castor oil the best option?
Answer: None f those will help with true dandruff. You need Tea Tree oil. It has anti microbial properties that will control the dandruff microbes. Provided you actually have dandruff and not dry scalp which is a totally different condition. Stay away from olive oil on the scalp. We use olive oil in the lab to grow specific micro organisms in petrie dishes.

Question: Why is my chemical-free TRESemmé shampoo not lathering?

Question: How can you distinguish between natural and dyed hair in older individuals? What are some indicators that reveal the difference?
Answer: Look for roots, just like you do in younger individuals. The whiter gray the hair is, the more contrast there will be. A lot of people with gray hair opt for a lighter color than they had in their youth so there is less contrast when the hair grows out.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: What causes the difference in hair texture among black women?
Answer: Genetics plays a major role in hair texture regardless of your race. The circumference of the hair is going to be fine medium or course. You can have fine medium and coarse Textures in every ethnicity. Then we break it down into how straight wavy or curly the hair is. Circumference is going to be decided by the size of the actual hair follicle and how fine or fat the hair is growing from said follicle. Actual textures are going to be decided by the shape of the hair follicle. If the hair follicle is perfectly round, it's going to produce straight hair. Oval follicles produce wavy hair. Flat follicles produce highly textured curly and kinky hair. Follicles you are born with we're passed down to you from your parents, grandparents, great grandparents, etc.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: What is the best way of washing hair styling products from our hair when using on a daily basis?
Answer: Using daily hair styling products will cause a buildup over time. The newer sulfate-free shampoos don't have the strength to break down the resins in specific adhesive and cohesive ingredients used in Hairspray and styling products. I suggest getting a clarifying shampoo and clarifying your hair once every 6 or so shampoos. Clarifying shampoos are strong enough to break down the buildup and should not be used as a daily shampoo as the pH is too high for the scalp in hair for daily use.

Question: What are the effects of putting bleach over already bleached blonde hair?

Name: Jo Welch
Question: What is the difference between a hair salon and a beauty parlor? Are they both used for hair services?
Answer: Beauty parlor is just an old fashioned name for a hair salon. Beauty parlors were tied to the ladies and barber shops were tied to men. Over the years we've seen a lot less Beauty parlors and more family hair salons who cater to the needs of everyone. Barber shops seem to have an uptrend because of all the really cool Clipper cuts that are back in style. When Beauty Parlor was the term used for hair salons we cosmetologist and hair stylists were referred to as beauticians. In the 70s we saw a new animal in hair care. They were called unisex hair salons. This is when the shift started with a Barber named Sam in Memphis, Tennessee who opened one of the first full service family haircare salons. Before the Inception of full service salons who catered to both male and female, children would get their haircut with their dad at either the barbershop or with Mom at the beauty parlor. Sometimes these kids would get some pretty unattractive haircuts because they were going to Cutters who specialized in gender-based cutting and styling. When little girls would go with their dads to the barber they ended up with some pretty ugly haircuts. When longer masculine hairstyles hit the market (Good example was the Beatles and the Monkeys rock stars), Moms were taking little boys to the beauty shop because Barbers didn't know how to do this type of work. Back to Sam the barber, who was talented and could do all sorts of hair cuts not just Clipper cutting. The trend took off and the first “Fantastic Sams” family salon opened in Memphis. Other companies would follow suit. And it was also the beginning of franchise salons. Many are still here including Fantastic Sams. Supercuts has been around for years. One of the ones that did not survive was Command Performance Cuttery. We also have Great Clips, we have Sport Clips and many, many more franchise companies that cater to both men and women and children.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Can a 14-year-old get their hair cut by themselves or would they have to be accompanied by an adult?
Answer: This is going to depend entirely on Salon policy because there are no laws on age limits for children being accompanied by a parent during a hair service. Our policy is; parent or Guardian must be present during the haircut and agree to the service to be performed before services are started. Question: Why isn’t the brand HI LIFT hair dye covering my greys? I’m 100% and following the instructions. I’m using 6/00+6/3. I have tried different formulas to try fix this problem. Including adjusting ratios. Should I just go boring 6/00? Will it look flat?

Oils will also help create a barrier so styling products do not stick to your hair and are easy to remove versus building up over time. If you put a permanent wave on top of the bleached hair you have an 80% chance of losing 80% of that bleached hair. If you find someone that is really knowledgeable and has a great deal of expertise in perming bleached hair, they will take the steps necessary to keep the hair from dissolving. With that being said, someone super ultra Savvy who is capable of doing this can give you two choices. A very mild perm that's going to relax considerably on the hair that's previously bleached. Question: Can Apple cider vinegar promote healthy, long-lasting hair growth? If so, how often should one apply ACV to their scalp in order for it to be effective?

Apple cider vinegar due to its lower pH, used on a regular basis can be highly corrosive to the hair. A better option for strong hair growth is to massage your scalp approximately 10 to 15 minutes twice a day to promote circulation to the hair follicles. You will get more of a hair growth benefit from a firm but gentle scalp massage than you will from any hair conditioner. Conditioner will maintain your hair and keep it healthy but does not promote follicular health.

Question: Does copper sulfate have any effect on colored hair?
Answer: Copper sulfate is added to the ingredients that go into swimming pool chemicals. It is an excellent algaecide chemical used to destroy algae. When you go swimming the chlorine in the chemicals break down the hair and the hair will absorb copper sulfate. When you get out of the pool and let your hair dry, the copper sulfate will get trapped in the hair. Over time it will oxidize and turn green. Think of the Statue of Liberty. She is made of copper and therefore she oxidizes and turns green too. The best way to keep this from happening to your hair, is to cover your hair before you get in the pool. If this is an extreme fashion faux PA for you, wet your hair thoroughly with tap water before you enter the pool. Upon leaving the pool immediately go to the shower while your hair is still wet and shampoo it. Another trick is when you wet your hair down, coat it liberally with an inexpensive type of heavy conditioner. You still have to shampoo your hair immediately upon leaving the pool though. There is a treatment that will remove copper buildup from the hair. Malibu C crystal gel treatment. It requires dryer heat. Call around and find a salon that uses it. Have the treatment done and go home with a swimmer's hair kit also made by malibu.

Question: How long does it take for coconut oil to get rid of dandruff naturally at home without shampooing your hair or going to the parlor every time?

Both have antimicrobial properties that will slow down the reproduction of the microbes that cause dandruff. Dry flaky scalp on the other hand is a completely different condition. Coconut oil does not have the ability to moisturize anything. You can use it on top of a moisturizer to help seal it in, but coconut oil is not a moisturizer. If you have dry scalp use something formulated for dry scalp. Stop the kitchen preparations, you can actually get yourself in worse shape by listening to these bloggers that have no knowledge of skin conditions, scalp conditions. Some of the oils I have seen mentioned for home hair and scalp preparations are actually used in labs to grow microbes. If you don't know what you are using and how it can actually work as food for specific microbes, you can make a condition worse.

Question: What is the best over-the-counter treatment for dandruff and dry scalp?

Question: I went into the pool a day after my perm, is it bad? I mean it’s still curly right now, but it's not as curly as the day I got the perm. Is there any way to make it really curly?

During this time the perm is still oxidizing and hardening. You disrupted that cycle by adding a chemical to your hair. So the best thing you can do at this point is to try to get the chlorine out of your hair because it's going to continue to do what it does. Perms relax naturally over time. Exposing a fresh perm to any of the things I mentioned above will prematurely and permanently relax the curl pattern. Anyone reading this for future reference please the recommended time before doing any of the above to your fresh perm. If you're going to get in a chlorinated pool, I'm talking after the hair has oxidized and for anyone getting in a chlorinated cool regardless of what's on their hair. It's always better to wet the hair down with fresh water before entering the pool. After exiting the pool while the hair is wet shampoo and condition immediately. If you let chlorinated water dry in the hair it leaves behind cool chemicals. Question: Should I go back to the salon to ask for a fix if my color correction is fading within a few washes? My hair was botched, bleached white, fried. I had lowlights and toner added to hide the blotchy spots but now the color is awful.

Question: What is the best semi-permanent hair dye that will cover grey, be long lasting, and not damaging to the scalp or cause breakage in newly grown hair?

Question: What is your opinion on shampoo samples? Do you think they are effective? Do you have a preferred brand?

Question: How much does it cost to buy a Great Clips franchise, and how long does it take to break even after buying the salon?
Answer: There are so many variations in play here, you are best to reach out to Great Clips directly. You have franchise fees franchise licenses and also your build out to consider. I'm not sure what their franchise fees are. Oftentimes they're based on a percentage of sales not profits. Franchise licenses and sales can be expensive and another reason why you should reach directly out to Great Clips. I've worked with another franchise company for years and very knowledgeable how it plays out. First you sit down with the franchise company to see if you are financially in a place to do this. Things are going to be considered like your personal assets and income, credit score, etc. Franchise fees can run anywhere from 5% to 10% depending on the company. Cost for your upfront license is a determination with the franchise company. 25 to maybe $35,000 is just a rough estimate of what it might be for the cost of your franchise license. Then you have your Salon location build out. That can run you up to 200 Grand. You have to have enough working capital to pay your employees until they are making money and paying you. Say you open a new business and you hire a new staff. They have no clientele, you have no clientele. You might open with weekly sales under $2,000 and have to pay your staff minimum wage out of that $2,000. Staff is going to eat up half of your cash flow. Every dollar you have coming in the door, 50 cents I is going to go to pay employee payroll, employee taxes, unemployment insurance, liability on said employees. And if your weekly franchise fee is say 10%, 200 goes to Great Clips for the week. So if you did have a low $2,000 a week, $1,000 goes back to your payroll, 200 gets direct drafted from your account to Great Clips to pay for your weekly franchise fee. This leaves $800 for the week. Times that by 4 weeks. Subtract your rent of approximately $2,000, subtract your build out loan payment of approximately $2,000. And we're not even looking at all the utilities or supplies needed to run to business. Then you have your advertising fund. There's other hidden costs here like accounting, payroll miscellaneous Sundries, liability insurance. As time goes by and you keep staff in place, your clientele will build and your cash flow will increase. A $2,000 a week is going to keep you in the hole. You will have to keep dipping into funds until you can bring that number up significantly. Understand the figures I'm giving you above or rough estimates. Your salon may come out of the gate making more a week or less. Building a salon business is a Snowball Effect. I have seen salons start out with 1,500 to 2,000 a week grow quickly to 10,000 a week. I've seen the same owners with Salon locations that started out with unheard of and amazing success in numbers. And it was all in the location. The same owners could go out and start another franchise salon at a new location and have it totally bomb. There's no way of knowing exactly how successful you will be until you have made the investment and started the business. I knew a guy who started a Supercuts franchise with his 401k after he left his company. He knew nothing about the industry, except he had a friend that owned a couple of them and told him it was a good investment. This man with no knowledge and the support of the franchise company turned one Salon into 50 salons. He eventually sold those salons back to the company at a good profit and moved into another endeavor. Your location and ability to hire and keep the staff are going to be crucial to your success. Great Clips will provide you with a lot of tools to run your business and advertising packages to get you up and running. I've seen salons turn a profit and as little as 2 years but expect to spend five years in the hole or breaking even. That first five years you are paying for the construction site build out. In addition to the construction site build out you will have a rent payment. Most Great Clips go into existing shopping centers with a large anchor store if they're lucky. An anchor store would be something like a large supermarket that brings in a lot of people. Staffing has been a struggle since covid. A lot of cosmetologist did not go back to work because they found it profitable to do hair at home under the table. An illegal practice, but people were desperate when everything shut down and we're doing anything they could regardless of safety issues to get their hair done. Please reach out to corporate Great Clips as they can give you an entire business plan and help you locate a good site with favorable demographics to pull in the clientele. You do not necessarily have to be a licensed cosmetologist to own a great clips. But I find it helpful in the very beginning because if you are short of staff, you can roll your sleeves up and pitch in. There is a Formula out there that states you need three franchise locations in order to quit your day job.

Question: My hairdresser washed my hair right after curl perming my hair. She also blow dried my hair. Did she do the right thing? I don’t think she should’ve done those?

After the required processing time, the hair is rinsed thoroughly with the rod still in place. Towel blotted very well and a neutralizer is applied for approximately 5 minutes. After this time, the rods will be removed and the hair will be rinsed thoroughly. Shampoo is not part of the step. For longevity it is preferred the hair be rinsed thoroughly and if there's any type of conditioner added it will be something required by the manufacturer after the permanent wave is completed. Perms will hold up longer if they are allowed to dry naturally immediately after the service. You are not to shampoo your hair for a minimum of 72 hours, which makes me wonder why your hair with shampooed after your perm. The hair is under fragile state immediately after and I prefer not to use Heat until the 72-hour period is over. I am thinking that maybe the individual who did your perm, drop the rods and panic because they thought it was too curly. So in order to relax it a little bit this individual shampooed your hair, and used heat to style it. Or, they just don't have any sense and I see a lot of that in our industry. Question: Does a sulfate free shampoo cause your scalp to itch?

Question: I bleached my hair blonde and then dyed it orange, but now I want to go back to blonde. Will my hair fall out if I bleach it?
Answer: Let's talk a little bit about color chemistry. First you bleached your hair which removed all the pigment from it and compromised the structure and integrity. Cuticle layers will never actually lay completely flat again. I'm going to assume you put a fashion color to get the orange. Fashion colors do not require hydrogen peroxide. They are pretty much direct eyes that put a deep stain on the exterior of the hair. A very savvy colorist knows not to put bleach on top of bleached hair with fashion colors. First rule of thumb is never apply bleach on top of previously bleached hair. Second rule of thumb is fashion colors were never designed to sit anywhere but on the exterior part of the hair shaft. Applying bleach on top of a fashion color will push the fashion color deeper into the hair and make it impossible to remove. You need to see a good colorist with the skills and various products at their fingertips needed to remove the orange color and prepare the hair. This person will use whatever products needed to handle going back to blonde. There is a possibility you may never go back to blonde without growing it completely out and cutting it off. There is a possibility you may have a slight orange tint to your blonde hair regardless of what you try to do. Hair color is not like putting on a different pair of shoes. You are dealing with chemistry that tears the hair down. Hair be repaired 100%. Sometimes it is more of a matter of keeping what you have until you can grow it out. It is much easier to color over fashion colors with a darker level than it is to pull fashion colors out and make the hair blonde again.

Question: There's a question I can't seem to get a straight answer on. Does using "baby shampoo" (let's use Johnson & Johnson formula) strip hair color from hair better than others or is it the safest gentlest on it? I was told it removes it like no other.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Is baby shampoo good for dry eyes?
Answer: I am not a physician but I've had a battle with dry eyes for several years. Dry eyes could be caused from lack of tear production or lack of oil duct production. We all have tiny little oil ducts that line our eyelids that help to lubricate our eyes. The best thing to do is use a warm compress for a minimum of 10 minutes per night. If you have time you can do this up to three times a day. They actually sell little units that heat up for you to do this with. But I have a buckwheat eye mask. I heat it up for 30 seconds in the microwave, shake it around and heat it up again for another 30 seconds. If this is not the problem, you need to be adding an eye lubricant. This can be in the form of drops, gel or ointment. The only thing you would be using baby shampoo for is to gently cleanse the eyelids to help remove any debris that could be blocking your oil ducts. Baby shampoo is really not good for the skin or the hair. The pH is too high for the skin to use daily. But the pH matches the eye pH and that's why it does not burn and is good to cleanse around the eyes occasionally. Please see an eye doctor to determine if your dry eyes is caused by low tear production or low oil production. Usually if it's low oil production you might have a history of eye styes from blockages in the oil ducts. You want to make sure to use some sort of lubricant in your eyes before you go to bed. Stay away from the types of drops that people use to make their eyes look whiter. They tend to cause additional discomfort.

Question: I have a red/dark purple colour in my hair now. If I bleach it 40 developer, what colour will it turn?

Question: How old do I have to be to get a straight hair perm?

This is why sometimes you see children who start out with blonde hair and become brown hair. Or have curly hair that goes straight. Or straight hair that goes curly. Question: Do developers and hair color brands have to match? For example, I have Clairol Demi perm developer and Mystic Divine demi perm color.

Question: How do you tell people you don’t cut black hair politely?
Answer: All of us in the industry excel in some areas more than others. The best thing you can do is what I have done in the past with other services that weren't necessarily due to ethnicity as I am sure is the same with you. It isn't your area of expertise and you struggle with getting good results. I've never been really great at flat tops. I'm so glad they're not in Vogue anymore. We had a cutter in our salon who did beautiful flat tops. Anytime I would get someone in my chair who wanted a flat top I would politely say “Karen is our flat top specialist, she does flat tops better than anyone else in the salon. If you wouldn't mind waiting a few minutes I can get you in with her because I want you to love your hair today”. They would always want to wait the extra time to get in with Karen since I gave her such high accolades. This got me off the hook of doing a clumsy inadequate job and at the same time I didn't come off as being a snob that did not want to do their hair. So, if you get someone that has highly textured hair and you're not good at it, you do the same thing I did. You let them know that you have an expert in the salon who does exceptional work with highly textured hair and you want them to love their hair today. Question: What part should I do if I'm dying my hair a different shade of blonde? Where do I start at and how long do I leave it on with 40 volume (it's two to one)?

Question: Why does coconut oil not work as a deep conditioner for some people's hair?
Answer: Coconut oil will not work as a deep conditioner on anyone's hair. It is an oil with no conditioning properties. Oils sit on top of the hair. The best way to use any oil is to condition your hair by moisturizing and or adding a protein mask. Rinsing, towel drying the hair and adding a few drops of oil to the hair. This will help to hold the moisture from your conditioner in the hair. Applying oils first will block any moisture or protein you try to infuse into the hair. Coconut oil is not a good oil for hair. You want something lightweight like argan oil, Silk Oil or black seed oil. But remember, oils are not conditioners, oils will coat the surface of the hair each hair strand and then scalp. Using them sparingly will give your hair with a lot of shine provided you have conditioned before using an oil.

Question: How do I properly infuse dry rosemary and olive oil for hair growth?

Using heat on the scalp, both of these acts will bring blood to the scalp and therefore feed the hair follicle. If you want to grow hair use one of the tried and true brands scientifically proven to grow hair. Bosley is one of them, Revita and Nioxin are good also. If you using olive oil on the hair, use it very sparingly after conditioning and towel drying your hair and before applying any styling products. The same goes for rosemary oil. Dry Rosemary doesn't have much oil in it but it does have a nice fragrance. Adding it to olive oil won't do much more than give it a nice fragrance. It's best used to season poultry and beef while cooking. And that goes for olive oil too. Home hair remedies rarely give the results you get from professional products that have been tested over and over again for performance and improving or restoring the Integrity of the hair. If smashing up dry Rosemary and putting it in olive oil was that amazing for the hair, you would see hair product companies lining retail shelves with it.

Question: Can I mix water in blonde powder bleach with 40 developer to dilute developer? On package it says mix one sachet with one bottle of developer so I’m thinking 2 satches one bottle and the same amount of water as per bottle?

Question: What should I do if a perm came out too curly and I wanted wavy? Should I reperm with a bigger rod? If so, how long should I wait to do that?
Answer: The best thing you can do right now is wait. The curl pattern is going to drop over time. Give it a good 2 weeks. But for right now get yourself a nice heavy conditioner, clarify your hair with a good clarifying shampoo, apply conditioner and cover with a plastic processing cap. Use Heat for at least 10 minutes. If you don't have access to a cap dryer you can use a blow dryer or take a very steamy towel and lay it over the top of the processing cap. You can leave the conditioner on your hair longer than 10 minutes but at least give 10 minutes with heat to penetrate the cuticle and soften it. Sometimes this will help drop a perm. Whatever you do, if anyone suggests taking perm solution and combing through your hair, do not do that. It will not look pretty, it does not evenly relax the perm. After you have done the above with the conditioner and you still don't think in two weeks time your perm has relaxed enough you can reperm it with a larger rod. Make sure the perm you use is not an alkaline wave. You want to use a thio base perm. The reason why I suggest using a thio perm or an acid balanced perm as they are known in the business, is because it is a gentle perm. You are applying an additional chemical service over an already existing chemical service. This alone is going to increase damage to the hair. Nothing you can do about that at home. In the salon, we have goodies that we can use with our perms to protect the hair, products you do not have access to. Also, in the salon we have licensed cosmetologists that will tell you they can comb perm solution through your hair and relax it. Please trust me when I tell you that is not a good idea. I was a subject matter expert for cosmetologists all over the United States working with permanent waves. I also was an educator for a manufacturer who made permanent waves. My job was to teach cosmetologists how to use them correctly. There's not many out there like me left because we were heavy into the industry when perms were big before the big shift to hair color. Cosmetologist who have been coming out of school the last 15 or so years are not exposed to the generous number of permanent waves that the older stylists received back in the day.

Question: How often should you apply permanent hair coloring?
Answer: Rule of thumb is you want to retouch the new growth every 4 to 6 weeks. It is important for you to only apply the color to the retouch area. If you apply it over the previously colored hair, the previously colored hair will become darker. What happens over time when you overlap color, your new growth will appear lighter because the previously colored hair will continue to darken. If you do this correctly and apply only to the new growth you will have pretty hair color and it will be more likely to maintain its vibrancy. In the event you feel the ends are fading you can purchase what is known as a color enhancing shampoo or conditioner to keep the midshaft and ends vibrant. They come on many colors. My personal favorite is CHI Color Illuminate. The most common mistake I see in the salon and, people doing hair at home, is applying color from Roots to ends every time they color. The color starts looking dark and dull The roots look funky because they don't match the rest of the hair. Once you've done this a couple of times it is almost impossible for a colorist to remove the buildup of color on the ends. It requires several steps to correct and color correction is a premium priced service in salons.

Question: Is it safe to dye your own hair at home if you have naturally dark brown/black hair and want to lighten it to a brown shade?

Question: If I have 20 and 5 volume developer, how do I mix 10 volume for a demipermanent hair color?
Answer: Ten volume is not a demi-permanent color. 10 volume will give you a permanent hair color. Permanent hair color stays in the hair and grows out leaving a line of demarcation. We use 10 volume for same level or darker to deposit color. You need about 4.5 volume to 7 volume developer for a true Demi color. Just go buy what you need. Mixing five volume with 20 volume will give you a higher volume than the 10 volume. Equal parts will give you 12.5 volume hydrogen peroxide. Again, purchase the correct developer for the Demi color you are using. Demi - color will last up to 25 shampoos. It never really completely washes out hence the name Demi-permanent color. It will lose its vibrancy and leave a slight line of demarcation where it grows out. Another thing you could try would be to cut your 20 volume down to a 10 volume and shorten your processing time. The color will have a processing time in the directions. You may cut that processing down to anywhere from 50% to 75%. The only way to know is to do a strand test by mixing a little color and developer and applying it to a couple of sections of hair and timing it. To make 20 volume a 10 volume, simply mix equal parts 20 volume hydrogen peroxide with hair conditioner and make sure it is exactly the same measurements. By leaving the color on a shorter period of time, less pigment penetrates the hair hence creating a demi-permanent effect. If you leave it on the entire time you get permanent color because you get a higher percentage of oxidation of color inside the hair shaft.

Question: Do I use regular Clorox bleach with my hair dye to get deep burgundy color on my natural African American black hair?

It dissolves all the hair off the brushes and makes them beautifully clean. Clorox bleach is not the same as hair bleach/lightner. Hair bleach must be added with hydrogen peroxide in order to activate it. Hair bleach is not added to hair color. You don't use hair bleach to dye your hair. You use hair bleach to make your hair lighter and remove pigment from it not add pigment to it. Read the instructions for the color you are using to know what you are supposed to do. If the color requires hydrogen peroxide 20 volume or 10 volume, follow instructions for mixing. Some colors such as a few of the demi-permanents and semi - permanents on the market require no hydrogen peroxide because they do not penetrate the cortex. If you have African American hair, on a level scake from Level 1 to level 11. Your hair is probably about a level three. The hair color you choose has to be dark enough to show up on level three hair. Look on the box of color to see if it has a level number as well as a name as you stated such as “burgundy”. Your hair may require a slightly lighter level and 30 volume developer. 30 volume developer should only be used by licensed professionals. With that being said. With the lack of knowledge you have as far as what chemicals can be combined together, I suggest you see a professional colorist. This way not only will you have hair but you will have pretty hair.

Question: What is PPD in hair color?
Answer: Paraphenylene Diamine is an ingredient used in darker hair dyes to anchor color. The problem is, it has the highest allergen rate per capita, compared to other ingredients in haircolor. This does not necessarily mean you cannot have an allergic reaction to some other ingredient in color. And why colorists will often perform a skin test to rule out allergies before applying color. Do your best to find color that does not contain this ingredient. Most companies are steering away from using it and are using an alternate ingredient that does the same thing without the high rate of allergic reactions. Allergic reactions can be fatal as was the case of a lady in the UK who used a color containing Paraphenylene Diamine in its back about 10 or more years ago. It made global news. At this time many companies started looking for alternative ingredients.

Question: Want to do my first perm on short, fine flat hair. Is a standard cold wave the best way to create firm, defined, shiny curls? Will added heat from a hood drier help the perm take and stay tight longer?
Answer: I take it you are going to try to do this at home. First of all the type of chemistry used has everything to do with the type of hair you have. If you have fine hair or hair that has a tendency to be slightly on a fragile side you want to use an acid balanced perm. Acid waves, cysteamine perms and acid balance waves create soft shiny natural looking curls. An alkaline wave is a lot more aggressive and goes deeper into the hair breaking more bonds. For baby fine hair this could be a deal-breaker with the Integrity of your hair. Second and very important, you only use heat if it says to use heat in the instructions. Heat is used with true acid waves only. If you use Heat with an alkaline wave you are going to damage the hell out of your hair. The size of the curl is determined by the size perm rod you use and not the strength of the perm. The health of the hair is determined by using the correct chemistry for your hair type. Perms in general do not create shiny curls. In fact, the curlier your hair is the less likely it is to be shiny. Flat Smooth hair reflects more light. Curly hair will only reflect light on the high ends of the curl pattern and will absorb light in the low ends of the curl pattern. The looks you see in the magazines and on Pinterest and other online resources are not perms, a lot of the shine you're seeing is created with product and hot lights. If you don't believe me, take a walk in an area where there's all sorts of people and look at their hair. If the hair is in good condition you will see shinier hair with straighter hair and not so shiny with curly hair. Tight kinky coils have no shine at all. Any shine created is going to be done with application of oils and shiners. Most of the looks you see in Media are created with either curling irons or flat irons. They are not perms.

Question: I used a level 5-6 toner on a level 7. Why didn’t it work?
Answer: There is really no way to answer this question without a lot of information from you. When you say your hair was a level 7, what underlying tones were you seeing? And based on those underlying tones, what was the color of the level five or six toner used? Was it a level 5 toner or was it a level six toner? Your underlying pigment on your level 7 hair, did you see orange, did you see yellow orange also known as gold? Was your toner an Ash base, was your toner a beige base? No way to answer this unless we know what color you put it on and what color toner you applied. Toners and hair color are not like paint that you roll on the wall and you see the color. They work on what's known as the rate of absorption. Whatever is the color of the hair combines with whatever color you put on the hair. This is why we can take a light violet/ beige toner and put it on yellow blonde hair and get a light natural blonde versus a violet blonde. On the color wheel Violet is the opposite of yellow. And why the two combined together give a natural or what's known as neutral color. If someone truly wanted a violet color they would have to add more Violet to the formula to offset the rate of absorption with the existing yellow eating up the violet color applied to the hair. I'm hoping this makes sense.

Question: Do hair stylists always give their clients the advice they agree with, or do they sometimes listen to what the client wants and give that advice instead?
Answer: It should be a combination of both. If someone has realistic goals with the type of hair they have, it's very easy to execute what they are asking for. Provided they have photos and a good open-ended conversation with each other. If someone comes in with unrealistic goals and the stylist knows from experience what the client is asking for is unobtainable, this is when things change. An example is someone comes in with black box dye on their hair and they want to be a platinum blonde on the same day. There is a strong possibility this cannot occur and oftentimes the client doesn't want to come in for several sessions and take on the time and the cost to get it correct. The other part of this, has to do with whether or not the hair can handle multiple bleach applications and not break off. This is when the stylist steps in and helps the client find a compromise. “Obviously this hair is not going to go to platinum blonde before it breaks off so let's go to something lighter than what you have but not go in the direction of platinum blonde”. Another example would be someone who does not spend a lot of time on their hair, and will not spend a lot of time on their hair. This person will come in with something that is obtainable but not put the work into it at home to make it look that way every day. Then it becomes The Stylists fault because they did not explain thoroughly on the care involved prior to the new style and after with the correct products needed to maintain the look at home. I had a young girl who sat in my chair years ago and beside my station was a photo of a model with a blunt chin length bob. The young lady told me that it was exactly what she wanted. Her hair and facial features were perfect for the look and it was easy for someone in their early teens to maintain. I executed the haircut and I nailed it. When I looked up in the mirror she had one tear streaming down her right cheek. I asked her what was wrong and she said “I didn't think it was going to be this short”. I cut it to the exact length that was on the model's hair. As I said, I nailed the haircut. To this day I always ask “Are you sure you want to go to the length of this photo because this is where it's going to hit you”, and I will show them with my hand exactly where it's going to land after the haircut. So the young lady was not wrong but she did not taken to consideration what the length was going to be for her and since she told me it was exactly what she wanted that's exactly what I created for her. Communication is very important. You have to wear your hair every single day in the world will see it. Unlike clothes which you can change out if you do not like them. If you have super thick curly hair and come in with a sleek style, be prepared to do the work on the back end. If you come in with three hairs on your head and you want a voluminous look, your stylist May suggest something different because your hair texture and density will not support the style. Suggestions to anyone would be: Bring numerous photos or have them tagged on your phone to show your stylist. Show them photos that you like and photos of hair that you don't like. For instance if you like your hair all one length, and you like it cut straight across, show them photos of the back with that shape. Then show them photos with it pointed and rounded and tell them this is not what you want, you like to look of straight across. This goes for bangs too otherwise you come out with too thick of a bang, to thin of a bang, a choppy Bang or an overly blunt Bang. Of course, in the industry we refer to bangs as The Fringe area. One more thing that can happen is you may know exactly what you want, your stylist may know exactly what you want, but they may not have the skill to execute that particular type of haircut. Hair cutting is an art. Think of hair cutting as handwriting. All of us learn to write and some of us have beautiful handwriting and some of us do not. The same goes with hair cutting. Cosmetologists and Barbers both go to school and they learn how to cut. Hair cutting is just like handwriting. It's either pretty or it's not.

Question: How can you bleach bright red hair?

Question: I dyed my hair and I’ve been not touching my hair for like 13 months because of an allergy. What should I do?

I would do some research with the current you use on your hair 13 months ago and see if it contains an ingredient known as PPD or paraphernaline diamine. If you find this was in the color, you probably had a reaction to it. If you find this ingredient is not in the color your reaction was to some other ingredient and it's going to be hard to pinpoint what it is. What we do in the industry is if we suspect an allergy we do what's known as a skin test or patch test. We mix a small amount of all the ingredients that go into the color application for that client and apply it behind their ear and in the crook of their elbow inside. It stays there for 24 hours. If there is any reaction whatsoever we refrain from doing the service with that particular chemical color makeup. I advise that you stay away from hair color if you don't have the time to do a skin test. People die. Yes they do, they can go into anaphylactic shock and die from allergic reactions to hair color. There are documented cases. You could also have serious skin reactions that cause permanent scarring.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How does washing your hair less often increase its length and thickness?
Answer: It doesn't. You want a healthy scalp and clean hair. A healthy scalp creates healthy hair. Massaging your scalp thoroughly when you shampoo and condition increases blood flow to the scalp therefore feeding the hair bulb which in turn helps with hair growth. The less frequency in shampooing leads to more oil and debris buildup on the scalp.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How can I differentiate between real hair and synthetic?
Answer: Remove three strands of hair from the Swatch or wig and twist them together. Now you are going to take a match or a lighter and burn it. If it smells like burnt hair it's natural hair if it smells like burnt plastic it is synthetic.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: What is the best product to use on bleached/dyed hair to prevent fading and keep your colour longer than normal?
Answer: CHI Color Illuminate conditioners. They come in an array of colors. How they work is by depositing small amounts of direct dyes into the hair every time you can condition. At this time, you switch back over to your normal shampoo and conditioner until you see the need to reapply the color enhancing conditioner.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: What are the best chemical and natural ingredients in an anti-dandruff shampoo?
Answer: Look for shampoos containing pyrithione zinc, selenium sulfide or tea tree oil. Make sure you really have dandruff and not dry flaky scalp. The two are completely different conditions. Dry flaky scalp will be accompanied by small dry Flakes and an itchy scalp. Dandruff will be accompanied by largest yellowish colored flakes that are oily. Oftentimes they will peel away from the scalp in pieces as small as your pinky fingernail or as large as a quarter. If you have dry itchy scalp, look for moisturizing shampoos and conditioners instead.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Is it appropriate to tip your hair stylist if he/she was on his/her cell phone while cutting your hair?
Answer: I have a big issue with barbers and stylists talking on their cell phones while working on clients. It is unprofessional. You are paying for their time. You are not an interruption to their business. You are their business. You pay their bills. They should be devoting their time to you. They should be paying attention to what they are actually doing to avoid a mistake. If you simply do not tip and do not explain why, they will not catch on to the annoyance, shrug and continue the practice. Complain to management. If this person rents a space and you pay them directly - you complain to them. I have been in the industry since 1975. Shame on any licensed professional who does this to a paying client in their chair.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Will leaving an overnight hair mask on all night long damage our hair?
Answer: Is the mask you are using suggesting applying and leaving overnight? Most hair and scalp masks are going to do as much as they possibly can within the first 20 minutes. Anything more than that is overkill. Follow instructions as per manufacturer for best results. If it contains clay, as soon as it dries out it has done its job. If it contains clay, covering it with a processing cap and keeping it moist prevents the clay from drying and doing its job. Most ingredients in masks will not be harmful if left on past the required timing. They just don't do anything more after the required timing. I doubt you would get any damage.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: When you go to a barber shop, can you get a haircut and get your hair dyed at the same time?
Answer: You can, provided your Barber does color. Some states have what is known as a restricted barbers license. Barbara's carrying a restricted license are not covered to perform chemical services. Cosmetologist can do it all. A suggestion, instead of getting a permanent hair color go for a demi-permanent. This will grow out with less of a line of demarcation. If you wear your hair short, by the time you get ready for your next haircut it'll be time to do the color again. It's best to go a level or two lighter than your natural color, and blend your Grays rather than cover them. If you are covering gray hair. If you're just making your hair a different color you can go the same level or darker with a demi permanent but you cannot go lighter.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Can I get my normal hair back as I already started to regret doing permanent hair straightening yesterday?
Answer: Permanent hair straightening goes through a similar process as permanent waving. The hair bonds are broken down and while they are at their softest point, the hair is then neutralized at the broken down state into the new shape. This is an aggressive procedure and does create chemical damage. If you go back over with any other chemical, the damage could be severe enough to cause breakage. The first couple of weeks your hair will be straighter and over time it will revert back some. Any chemical service you do to try to recover your lost curls will result in additional damage - you cannot duplicate natural curl pattern chemically. Your best bet is to wait it out and grow it out. Straightening services are not the same as smoothing treatments. A straightening is a permanent change in the hair structure. Smoothing treatments are just that, treatments. You should have tried something in this category first to see if it was something you really wanted to do. Smoothing treatments can slightly relax hair. But the biggest benefit of a smoothing treatment is less expansion of the hair and frizziness can be removed up to 95%. A smoothing treatment can last anywhere from 2 to 4 months. A permanent straightener has to grow out and will leave a line of demarcation where the straight hair ends and the new curly hair that grows out begins. Try some deep conditioning. Use good moisturizing products. I personally like to use Chi Olive and monoi oil shampoo and conditioner on straightened hair as well as relaxed hair.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Can I do a color remover on a black box dye without it ending up patchy?
Answer: The only way to find out is to do what professional colorists do. Take a section of hair and apply the Color Remover from Roots to ends. Follow instructions. See what the results are. We do this versus dumping it all over the head and finding out on the back end we've created a bigger mess. Sometimes we have to say no. Sometimes the only way to say no is to show them what in the heck will happen if things go south. Good luck.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How can I take a spoonful of olive oil without it burning my throat?
Answer: Mix it with some balsamic vinegar and a little bit of salt pepper and garlic. Put it on a salad.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: My natural black hair is turning brown and dry after half a year of using a hair straightener. How do I retrieve my natural hair colour back?
Answer: Other than dye your hair there's not much else you can do. If you want to prevent this from happening to your new hair as it grows out. There are some things you need to do to protect your hair from heat. First of all, always use a thermal protecting spray that has some dimethicone or cyclomethicone in it. This will hold in moisture and keep out Heat. Drop the heat setting on your hot tools. Only use as much heat as you need to do the job. The higher the heat the more damage and lightening will occur. Do not pass the same areas over and over with a curling iron or a flat iron. Your heat setting should be set to where you only need to make one or two passes moving at about 1 inch per second. Use a good moisturizer on your midshaft and ends every time you shampoo your hair. Avoid sunlight as much as possible as this helps to lighten the hair too. If you make these changes, when your hair grows out, it will not lighten as much. Another thing to mention is, do not be using Hot Tools on your hair everyday if you can avoid it. Consider having a chi Enviro smoothing treatment. It will keep your hair smoother and frizz free for a minimum of 90 days. This will allow you to not need to use as high a heat on your hair. If you do decide to dye your hair the least damaging thing you can do would be either a semi-permanent or a demi-permanent versus using a permanent color with a higher volume of developer. It will not last as long but it will not break down the hair as much as permanent color will. Understand too the color you use is artificial and will never perfectly match your natural hair color.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: I am 13 and I started to get anderarm hair. What should I do?
Answer: You have two options. Remove it or leave it there. If you live in the US, popular culture here is to remove it. This can be done with shaving, waxing or using a depilatory agent. Ask your parents or parent if they are okay with you removing the hair because it bothers you, once you start shaving it or removing it in any way it grows back more stubbly. It will not grow back thicker. But as you get older you may find you have hair your armpits then you do at 13 years old. Hormones kick in. Superfluous hair follicles wake up. Females oftentimes remove it but I also know of men who shave their armpits as well as chest hair.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: If I don’t wash my hair after dying it, how long will it last?
Answer: It will last a lot longer if you rinse it thoroughly with very warm water and shampoo it twice. Followed by an acidic conditioning treatment. If you just rinse your hair dye provided you are referring to an aniline derivative dye - requiring hydrogen peroxide, you risk having extreme scalp irritation and it's going to fade really fast. BUT - If you are referring to a direct dye that does not require oxidation (peroxide) as in “fashion colors”, you would do well to rinse it very well with cold water and not shampoo. Following up with an acidic conditioner. The most important thing is that you follow manufacturers instructions for the particular hair dye you are using. All can vary. So it's difficult to give you advice when there are literally hundreds upon hundreds of different makers of hair dyes. Some requiring shampooing and others requiring only rinsing. It all depends on the chemistry.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Will a perm work on damaged hair?
Answer: Since permanent wave solution damages hair in its own right, if the hair is too damaged a perm is not recommended.

Question: What color will my golden blond hair fade too if I use a semi-permanent natural dark brown to match my roots as I grow out my hair?
Answer: No one here can answer your question. It's going to be a guesstimation. All depends on how porous your hair is and whether or not you use a sulfate free shampoo. Fading can also be accelerated by using Hot Tools and getting in the sun. All I can say is do it and wait and see what happens. Semi-permanent color lasts up to 12 shampoos. But this does not mean it's going to all come out.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: I accidentally washed a bit of my hair with mouldy rice water. What do I do? It smells.
Answer: Put some vinegar in a spray bottle. Wet your hair down, squeeze any excess moisture out. Spray the hair generously with the vinegar and comb it through. Leave it on your hair about 10 minutes. Shampoo and condition as you normally do. This should do it. If it doesn't, you can do something which is a little more abrasive to the hair. Mix a couple of teaspoons of baking soda with shampoo in your palms work together well wet hair down, and shampoo mixture in thoroughly. Try the vinegar one first it's easier on the hair.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How do I remove the tea tree oil smell from my hair?
Answer: Try using a clarifying shampoo. Leave it on your hair for 10 minutes, rinse and follow up with a regular shampoo and conditioner. If this doesn't work, mix a tablespoon of baking soda in your hand with regular shampoo. Massage thoroughly into your hair. Rinse, shampoo and condition.

Question: Can hair spray make a fire alarm go off?
Answer: I don't know about a fire alarm, but I know any type of aerosol spray will set off a carbon monoxide alarm. Has everything to do with the ratio of Clean Air versus particles. I have never had it occur with pump Hairspray. It has always been with aerosol type sprays because they disperse into the air where the pump spray particles drop to the ground.

Question: I accidentally bought 2 conditioners, is there a way I could turn one into shampoo?

Question: Dandruff keeps showing back only in the front of my head. I have used coconut oil and lemon this winter and it helped. What do I do about the front?

Question: If I pluck every baby hair and widows peak hair, would the hair be permanently gone? Can someone explain the biology/science of plucking forehead hair? I want laser but can't afford it. I know plucking ruins the hair follicle eventually.

Question: No matter how many times I wash my hair (I tried every 3 days and every day) and no matter how much products I use, it’s always itchy. What am I doing wrong?

Is your scalp itchy and dry or is your scalp itchy and oily. If it's itchy and dry it could be something as simple as changing to a moisturizing shampoo and conditioner. If it's itchy and oily you can have anything from dandruff, seborrhea to psoriasis. It could also be an allergy to the products you are using. It could be one specific ingredient and either the shampoo or conditioner, or it could be the fragrance. Yes fragrance allergies can not only affect your respiratory system but also itchiness of your scalp. Paul Mitchell has one, but my favorite one is the CHI tea tree line it is more prescriptive and I've had really good results using it on individuals with dry itchy scalp as well as mild dandruff. If you use a blow dryer and you get it too close to the scalp you can dry your scalp out and have itchy spots. I have done this to myself. Name: Jo Welch
Question: How much time does it take permanent highlights for hair to fade?
Answer: Highlights do not fade. Highlights involve removing color from strands of hair by bleaching or any other type of hair lightning. The color has been removed so therefore it can't fade. It can take on a darker appearance from hard water deposits or well water. But you can't have a fade of color where there is no color involved. It will need to grow out and you will have roots. We call that new growth. There is a way to get rid of them though, you can color over the top of them. I do not suggest doing this at home because if it is really blonde it may take on hair color differently than natural pigmented hair that is non- porous. It has to be formulated to put back what's missing, orange and gold. Even if you do not want gold it has to be added back because it was bleached out. A tube of brown color does not know what type of hair it is going on. This determination is made by the colorist as to what needs to be added to an already formulated one size fits all tube or bottle of color that may need tweaking a bit.

Question: What is the difference between a lightener and bleach for hair?

Question: Can I brush my hair wet while in the shower, or will it damage it?

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Can I wash my hair with cold water and conditioner everyday after bleaching it or should I just stay true to the wash your hair 1-2 times a week?
Answer: You do not necessarily need to use cold water. The only time we stress cold water is with the demi-permanent bright fashion colors. They fade off the hair really quick and warm water tends to break up that molecule more than cold water does and gives it some longevity. Cold water helps with fading. You should be shampooing your hair with warm water (not hot), this assists in breaking up dirt, oils and debris from the scalp. Apply conditioner followed by a Cool Water Rinse. How often do you shampoo your hair is determined by your hair type and the condition of your scalp. If you are using a really good moisturizing shampoo and conditioner, you can shampoo as often as you like. The real culprit is how much heat you apply to the hair after you shampoo. Heat grom styling tools is the second biggest killer of healthy hair. The first killer is chemical services. Especially overlapping chemical services. I find when I use sulfate free shampoos I can wash my hair more often because sulfate free shampoos don't remove natural oils and styling products as thoroughly as sulfate shampoos. So with that being said, I find when I use sulfate free shampoos on a regular basis, I must clarify my hair once every seven shampoos since sulfate free shampoos are too mild to remove buildup from products used for styling and hairspray.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: I have naturally black hair and recently I dyed it for the first time with a light brown dye, however, its not that noticeable. Should I dye it again, or what other methods can I do to get the shade a little browner?
Answer: Black hair can be a level 1, 2 or a level 3. This is important to know when lifting with hair color. It is very difficult to lift natural black hair more than one or possibly two levels using haircolor verses a bleach or non ammonia lightener. Doing so requires 40 volume developer with the hair color and a hair color at least three levels lighter than your starting level. Rule of thumb is, anytime you're lifting hair with hair color, it is best to start with natural level 5 at the darkest. Anything darker than a level five is going to be difficult to significantly lift with hair color. This is because darker levels have a lot of pigment in them and it takes a long time to get them out. If you were a level three, you could probably get it up to a level 5 Brown the first time. But now you have hair color on top of your hair and color will not lift color. You probably would have had better luck to going to a colorist. We have access to some beautiful high lift lighteners. My favorite when lifting black hair to Brown is CHI Infra High Lift Cream color. I can take dark hair and use 20 volume and get a beautiful brunette. They also have 3 shades of red formulated just for dark hair.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How many inches will hair grow in 1 month when you use coffee and shampoo once a week?
Answer: Hair grows approximately 1/2 inch per month regardless of what you put on it. You can ensure hair is strong by gently massaging 15 minutes per day. A good time to do this is when you shampoo and condition your hair. This will increase blood flow to the hair follicle and circulation plays a major part in hair growth.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How can I lighten my dark hair? I dyed golden blonde but had to colour black as there are educational purposes. Unfortunately the black colour is too unnatural and it is somehow too dark in sunlight. Please advise me how to lighten the dark colour.
