Doing this yourself could lead to a Crazy myriad of colors and more damage to your hair. Getting the color right is one thing saving the Integrity of the hair is another.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Can a toner be used without bleaching?
Answer: A toner is merely hair color. And yes, you can tone without bleaching. Provided the color you choose is the same level or darker than the hair you are putting it on. Otherwise you will see nothing. The whole idea behind toning hair, is to shift the color away from undesired undertones.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: My hair is orange after I bleached it once and I want a honey blonde. If I bleach it again, what colour will it be?

If you bleach it again - please use a lower volume of developer because now your hair is consider previously bleached and more porous than when you started. What level are you trying to achieve and what do you consider a honey blonde? What I am getting at - is when you finally get it to the correct level you are still going to be challenged with underlying raw pigment that may be light gold or pale yellow. You will still need to tone it to the color blonde you want to achieve.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Can I use a clipper for a lineup instead of a razor/trimmer?

Name: Jo Welch
Question: What will happen if I dont add B in the GARNIER products for hair dye in my delvoper A? Will the color just be white or what?

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How come I get a cold after I shampoo my hair?

Name: Jo Welch
Question: I use a conditioner made for curly hair on my straight hair since its all I have at the moment. Will it change my hair type? Should I stop using it if I want to keep my straight hair?

Name: Jo Welch
Question: If overtone is semi-permanent how come it stains hair?
Answer: It stains the hair because that's how semi-permanent color works. It is a topical stain on top of the cuticle. It will last approximately 12 shampoos. This does not mean it's all going to come out in 12 shampoos. It simply means the color will be less vibrant than it was on the day it was applied. Most of the time semi Permanent shampoos will completely come out of the hair. But a lot of the fashion colors do not. Especially on hair that is fragile and porous. I want to add to this; semi-permanent has the word “permanent” in it. This should be your clue that it's going to stay in the hair to some degree. If you want something that completely comes out use temporary colors not semi-permanent colors.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How do I reverse a perm?
Answer: If your perm was done within the last 72 hours, you can shampoo it with a clarifying shampoo and condition it. This will relax the perm a little bit. It's not recommended to reverse a perm, doing so requires an additional chemical service and the hair will never look the way it did prior to the perm. If it is a fresh perm it's going to be a lot curlier than you want it right now but it's going to relax a little bit over time. Your other option is to have it re-permed with bigger perm rods to loosen the curl. Hopefully the person doing this has enough common sense to know that the processing time will probably be half of what it was originally because your hair is now chemically treated.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: How do I fix a ball of matted hair? I really don't want to cut it out.
Answer: Instead of cutting it out why don't you try inserting a pair of scissors in and snipping inside the knot in about three different areas deep in the knot. Then you want to start working on the outside closest to the ends of your hair with a brush and slowly work the knot out. It could take an hour or maybe even longer depending on how bad than knot is.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Can you put permanent dye over color depositing conditioners like keracolor?
Answer: You can. But if I were going to do it and do it right, I would use a really good clarifying shampoo and leave it on your hair a minimum of 10 minutes before rinsing. This is to remove some of the direct dye from the conditioner. Condition your hair, dry your hair completely before applying color all over.

Name: Jo Welch
Question: Why does my hair have silicone build up when my products don't contain silicone at all?
Answer: There are plenty of hair products on the market that will build up on the hair. Silicone, primarily dimethicone, if used correctly will help to prevent buildup from styling products and hairsprays. Dimethicone is not water soluble but it is shampoo soluble. There are many resins in hairspray, gels and mouses that build up on the hair. Some products contain waxes and oils that will build up on the hair. It is important if you are using styling products that you clarify your hair with a good clarifying shampoo once every seven shampoos.
